headline: High: shared-state orchestration plus MCP/API tooling creates medium-to-high risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors; compliance risk is lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can ingest application-defined files/stdin and uses developer-wired tools; OpenMetadata exposes MCP server, APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks. That creates a plausible bridge where OpenMetadata content can flow into LangGraph nodes and be treated as instructions. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF LangGraph nodes read OpenMetadata webhook/event payloads as prompts or instructions
IF the deployment connects OpenMetadata MCP/API outputs into LangGraph tool inputs without provenance tagging
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields passed from OpenMetadata into LangGraph
Insert a prompt-injection sanitizer before any LangGraph LLM call
Tag all OpenMetadata-derived content as untrusted in the orchestrator
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in catalog text
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware routing between MCP/API outputs and agent prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph handles model provider API keys and broad network egress, while OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, memory, and tribal knowledge via APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. If shared workspace or graph state carries sensitive metadata, either side can expose it through outbound calls. The profiles do not show isolation, so the shared-data pathway is credible.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata data classes include secrets, regulated metadata, or internal tribal knowledge
IF LangGraph nodes forward shared graph state to model providers or external APIs
mitigations: Restrict LangGraph prompts to redacted metadata only
Block secrets and identifiers from OpenMetadata exports
Use separate service accounts and workspaces for each agent
Turn off outbound logging of full prompts and payloads
requires-engineering: add field-level DLP on graph-state handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; OpenMetadata exposes APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP, which can mutate shared backend resources. Even without explicit filesystem overlap, both can act on shared mutable state through orchestration and metadata services. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so conflict risk is real but not maximal.
conditions: IF both agents target the same metadata backend, queue, or workspace
IF LangGraph tools and OpenMetadata webhooks mutate the same records without locks
mitigations: Assign separate write scopes to each agent
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Disable concurrent mutation jobs during shared runs
Add optimistic concurrency checks on shared records
requires-engineering: implement resource locking for shared mutable objects

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework where node outputs can become downstream inputs, and OpenMetadata is built around context, lineage, and governance data. That makes it plausible for LangGraph to consume OpenMetadata outputs as authoritative context and propagate mistakes into later actions. No verification layer is documented in either profile, so the interaction is more than low risk.
conditions: IF LangGraph routes OpenMetadata outputs directly into later decision nodes
IF downstream nodes act on metadata assertions without human or programmatic verification
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action
Require citations or source IDs for OpenMetadata-derived claims
Mark OpenMetadata outputs as advisory, not authoritative
Add confidence thresholds before acting on metadata facts
requires-engineering: build a validation gate between the agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. OpenMetadata touches governance and memory-like data classes, while LangGraph handles application-defined graph state and model-provider keys, so compliance issues are possible if regulated data is routed through them. Because the mismatch is not evidenced, this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are stored in OpenMetadata and forwarded into LangGraph prompts or logs
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention guarantees not configured in either agent
mitigations: Document the data classes allowed in each agent
Keep regulated data out of shared graph state
Set explicit retention limits on logs and checkpoints
Review vendor residency and DPA terms before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
